s1.syndrome_frame: Acute peripheral vascular syndrome with transient ischemic changes and possible autoimmune component
salient_findings: Tingling and burning of both feet
Bluish discoloration, swelling, and blistering on the toes
key_facts: No unusual cold exposure or precipitating events
No known connective-tissue or autoimmune disease
No source for emboli on echocardiography and abdominal ultrasonography

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute peripheral vascular syndrome with transient ischemic changes and possible autoimmune component
salient_findings: Tingling and burning of both feet
Bluish discoloration, swelling, and blistering on the toes
key_facts: No unusual cold exposure or precipitating events
No known connective-tissue or autoimmune disease
No source for emboli on echocardiography and abdominal ultrasonography

shortlist.label: Raynaud's Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a lifelong history of Raynaud’s phenomenon

shortlist.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Positive antinuclear antibody titer and elevated complement C4 level

shortlist.label: Scleroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms and history of Raynaud’s phenomenon are consistent with scleroderma

shortlist.label: Antiphospholipid Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated DNase-B antibody and patient's symptoms of transient ischemic changes

shortlist.label: Thromboangiitis Obliterans
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's age, sex, and symptoms of peripheral vascular syndrome are consistent with thromboangiitis obliterans

raw.rationale: The patient's lifelong history of Raynaud's phenomenon and the presentation of bluish discoloration, swelling, and blistering on the toes, which resolved without any evidence of systemic disease or other autoimmune conditions, best supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: Although the patient has a positive antinuclear antibody titer, the lack of other systemic symptoms and negative work-up for other autoimmune conditions makes this less likely.

rejected.label: Scleroderma
rejected.why: There is no mention of skin thickening or other characteristic features of scleroderma, making this diagnosis unlikely.

rejected.label: Antiphospholipid Syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and laboratory results do not support this diagnosis, as there is no evidence of thrombosis or other characteristic features.

rejected.label: Thromboangiitis Obliterans
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with more severe ischemic symptoms and is often associated with smoking, which is not mentioned in the patient's history.
